title: CIS Controls Practitioner
summary: The CIS Controls Practitioner (CIS-CP) certification is issued by the Center for Internet Security (CIS) for hands on security staff who put the CIS Critical Security Controls into practice. It sits at a practical, early to mid career level and suits system administrators, security analysts, engineers and consultants who must reduce risk in real networks. It proves to an employer that you can read a control, design an implementation for your environment, and measure whether it works, rather than only quoting the control list. The exam tests the CIS Critical Security Controls version 8 through scenario based multiple choice items that follow the controls in order, and CIS publishes the exam blueprint with the domains set out below. Typical roles include security analyst, systems engineer, vulnerability management specialist and IT security consultant. This is an independent study guide that is not official CIS material; check the vendor's current blueprint before booking.

sources.label: Center for Internet Security certification programme

beginner.definition: The CIS Controls Practitioner (CIS-CP) is a certification from the Center for Internet Security (CIS). It tests whether you can apply the CIS Critical Security Controls. Those controls are a prioritised list of actions that protect a network. The exam is about doing the work, not only naming the controls.
beginner.whyItMatters: Many teams do not know which security task to do first. The CIS Critical Security Controls give a clear order. This certificate proves you can turn that list into real changes on real systems. Employers value this because it shows practical skill. It also helps you explain your security plan to managers in a simple way.
howItWorks: Download the official CIS Critical Security Controls and read the exam blueprint that CIS publishes.
Work through the controls in order, because the first controls remove the largest risks.
Study the three implementation groups, which sort organisations by size and risk.
Practise on a small lab, for example by taking an asset inventory or hardening a server.
Learn how to show progress, such as the share of assets that meet a control.
The exam is multiple choice with scenario questions, so read each one as a work problem, not as a memory test.
beginner.example: Suppose your manager says the company needs better security and asks where to start. You do not begin with a costly new tool. You first write down every laptop, server and cloud account the company owns, because you cannot protect what you cannot see. Then you check how many of those devices still use the default password. Those two steps come from the first few controls. A CIS-CP holder knows this order and can explain why it saves money.
takeaways: The controls are ranked, so learn why early controls matter more than later ones.
The exam asks how you would implement a control in a described environment.
Implementation groups help you choose controls that fit the size of the organisation.

objectives: Describe the purpose and structure of the CIS Critical Security Controls
Choose controls that match an organisation's size, risk and resources
Build and maintain an accurate inventory of hardware, software and data
Plan secure configuration and access control for common systems
Explain how logging, monitoring and response controls work together
Measure control coverage and report progress to management

chapters.title: Asset inventory and control
objectives: Build an inventory of hardware and software that stays accurate over time
Find unauthorised devices and software and decide what to do about them
Assign an owner to every asset and record its role in the business
Handle mobile devices, remote workers and personally owned equipment
Explain why an accurate inventory comes before other security work

chapters.title: Data protection
objectives: Create a data classification scheme that staff can apply
Set handling rules for each class of data, including storage and sharing
Plan encryption for data at rest, in motion and in use
Set up secure disposal of data and of the media that holds it
Keep a record of where sensitive data is stored and who can reach it

chapters.title: Secure configuration of assets
objectives: Establish and keep a secure baseline configuration for each asset type
Remove or change default accounts and passwords
Turn off services and features that the business does not need
Manage configuration changes so the baseline does not drift
Automate checks that measure compliance with the baseline

chapters.title: Continuous vulnerability management
objectives: Set up a routine that scans for vulnerabilities on a schedule
Score and rank findings so the most serious are fixed first
Track remediation through to closure and record exceptions
Handle vulnerabilities in third party and cloud services
Report vulnerability trends to management in plain language

chapters.title: Controlled use of administrative privileges
objectives: Inventory accounts with administrative rights and remove unneeded ones
Require stronger authentication for privileged accounts
Log and review administrative activity
Separate normal work accounts from administrative accounts
Manage privileged access for suppliers and temporary staff

chapters.title: Access control management
objectives: Create and remove accounts as staff join, move and leave
Apply least privilege so people hold only the access they need
Use central authentication and review access rights on a schedule
Manage passwords, keys, certificates and service accounts
Explain how identity management reduces the chance of a breach

chapters.title: Security awareness and skills training
objectives: Design awareness training that covers the main attack methods
Run exercises that test whether staff can spot a phishing message
Train staff to report incidents quickly and without blame
Measure whether training changes behaviour, not only completion rates
Adapt training for technical and non technical audiences

chapters.title: Security monitoring and defence
objectives: Collect logs from important systems in one place
Set alerts on activity that matters and reduce noise
Plan how the team will respond to a confirmed incident
Test detection and response through simple exercises
Keep evidence so an incident can be reviewed later
